study.title: Transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation for postoperative nausea and vomiting in patients undergoing craniotomy: A randomized controlled trial
study.comparator_class: Cut-wire no-current sham P6; both ondansetron8mg
study.independence: Linked Lv2021 manual acupuncture report cites same protocol; TEAS/sham appear distinct protocol arms, but allocation framework/amendments and shared-control overlap unresolved. No automatic independent counting of linked reports.
study.source_locations: Complete6-page source, visual Fig1 and Tables4–5; cited2013 protocol retrieved/read publisher.
study.identity_notes: Table3P=.047 versus text .47 (decimal error). Exclusion of motion-sickness history conflicts with Table2 positive history16/57 and16/58. 2013 five-arm protocol300 planned vs two-arm120 publication; protocol planned lost cases counted PONV, publication excluded5. No cumulative0–24h vomiting total; intervals cannot be added as unique patients. Rescue10mg IM tramadol unusual but printed twice; preserve pending clarification.

final.Shared-control / multi-arm issue: Cited five-arm protocol; two arms reported here. Linked manual-acupuncture cohort/control relationship unresolved.
final.Source-QC issue: Five post-randomization exclusions include one sham participant excluded specifically for vomiting caused by intracranial hypertension
